claims.claim: Texas Instruments supplies analog and embedded semiconductor functions that bridge physical sensors, power and control systems to industrial, automotive and data-center infrastructure; broad Q2 growth across those end markets supports continued structural relevance beyond a single compute cycle.

The 300mm manufacturing strategy can improve cost/control and domestic supply resilience, but its value depends on sustained utilization; underutilization is the successor bottleneck if industrial/automotive demand relapses.

risks.risk: Large manufacturing investment can become an underutilized fixed-cost burden if broad industrial and automotive demand recovery reverses.

unknowns.unknown: Current utilization and incremental returns on new 300mm capacity are not quantified in the reused evidence.

claims.claim: Q2 revenue and operating-profit growth show a strong current recovery, but cyclical analog demand can reverse; the main present challenge is whether utilization remains high enough to earn adequate returns on new manufacturing capacity.

The evidence supports manufacturing scale and cash generation but does not prove exceptional pricing power or current utilization economics; the thesis is falsified if demand relapses and new fabs remain persistently underutilized with weaker free-cash-flow conversion.

risks.risk: Cyclical demand relapse can expose fixed-cost underutilization and depress returns on the 300mm capacity build.

unknowns.unknown: Peer-relative utilization, current valuation and incremental fab returns remain outside Beta's evidence and belong to underwriting where applicable.
